title: Altered medial prefrontal-striatal connectivity and plasticity in humanized CBLN2 mice
title_zh: 人源化< i >CBLN2</ i >小鼠中内侧前额叶-纹状体连通性与可塑性的改变
abstract: Abstract Deciphering processes that are responsible for differences in brain development and architecture among species may provide clues to the species-specific program and may facilitate a mechanistic understanding of vulnerability to neuropsychiatric disorders. It has recently been shown that the promoter of the CBLN2 gene, which codes for a synaptogenic factor, cerebellin 2 (Cbln2), has a repressor element in mice but not in humans. A humanized mouse lacking this repressor (hCbln2) reproduces higher spine density in medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) neurons and higher corticothalamic connectivity observed in humans. Cbln2 is part of a trans-synaptic complex that includes glutamate delta-1 receptor (GluD1) and neurexins (Nrxn) (GluD1-Cbln2-Nrxn). Interestingly, we have previously reported a contrasting striatal patch-matrix expression pattern of GluD1 in mouse versus monkey, suggesting a potential role of the GluD1-Cbln complex in species differences. In this study, we examined the synaptic organization and function in the cortex and dorsal striatum of hCbln2 mice. Consistent with previous reports, hCbln2 mice exhibited increased vGluT1 expression in the mPFC, indicating enhanced intracortical connectivity. Electrophysiological recordings further revealed an increased mEPSC frequency along with a reduced mIPSC frequency in layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons, suggesting an increase in excitatory/inhibitory balance. These changes were accompanied by enhanced mTOR signalling and autophagic deficits in the mPFC. Contrasting synaptic changes were observed in the striatum with an increase in vGluT2 and a reduction in vGluT1, together with a decrease in GluD1-Cbln1 and an increase in hevin. Importantly, corticostriatal dysfunction characterized by a reduction in cortical contribution to mEPSCs and impaired DHPG-induced synaptic depression was observed in the hCbln2 medium spiny neurons. Further, hCbln2 mice displayed increased repetitive behaviour together with social and affective-like deficits, consistent with autism-relevant phenotypes. Collectively, these findings identify humanized Cbln2 regulation as a driver of divergent cortical and striatal synaptic remodelling, disrupted corticostriatal synaptic function, and behavioural abnormalities relevant to neurodevelopmental disorders.
abstract_zh: 摘要 解析导致不同物种大脑发育和结构差异的机制可能为物种特异性程序提供线索，并有助于深入理解神经精神疾病易感性的机制。最近已发现，编码突触生成因子小脑素2（Cbln2）的基因启动子在小鼠中具有抑制元件，而在人类中不存在。缺失此抑制元件的人源化小鼠（hCbln2）可复制人类中内侧前额叶皮层（mPFC）神经元更高的树突棘密度和更高的皮层-丘脑连通性。Cbln2是跨突触复合物的一部分，该复合物包括谷氨酸δ1受体（GluD1）和神经突触素（Nrxn）（GluD1-Cbln2-Nrxn）。值得注意的是，我们此前报告了小鼠与猿猴之间GluD1在纹状体的斑块-基质表达模式的差异，提示GluD1-Cbln复合物在物种差异中可能发挥作用。本研究考察了hCbln2小鼠皮层和背侧纹状体的突触组织与功能。与先前报道一致，hCbln2小鼠在mPFC中显示vGluT1表达增加，提示皮层内连通性增强。电生理记录进一步显示，2/3层锥体细胞的mEPSC频率升高，mIPSC频率下降，表明兴奋/抑制平衡倾向于兴奋性增加。这些变化伴随mTOR信号通路增强和mPFC自噬缺陷。纹状体中观察到相反的突触变化，vGluT2升高、vGluT1下降，以及GluD1-Cbln1下降、hevin升高。重要的是，hCbln2中间棘细胞表现出皮层对mEPSC贡献减少和DHPG诱导的突触抑制受损的皮层-纹状体功能障碍。进一步观察到hCbln2小鼠表现出重复行为增加以及社会和情感类缺陷，符合自闭症相关表型。综上所述，这些发现表明人源化Cbln2调控是驱动皮层与纹状体突触重塑差异、破坏皮层-纹状体突触功能以及与神经发育障碍相关行为异常的关键因素。
